sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 sits at 7,718.60, roughly mid-range (about 52% of its trailing month) and near 1% below its August highs -- no strong directional signal from the index itself. The Nasdaq 100 shows the same pattern: 29,544.15, mid-range, just under 2% off its recent peak. The VIX has drifted to 14.53, near the bottom of its one-month band, consistent with a market not pricing much event risk into the week. The Euro Stoxx 50 is the outlier, sitting near the bottom of its own one-month range at 6,392.93. This week's operating-entity reporting load is comparatively light -- 13 events in the SP500/R1000/core universe, concentrated on Thursday and skewed toward technology names.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tuesday brings Dell Technologies (DELL US) into a technology sector that has been essentially flat on reaction (+0.25% median across 535 names) -- no strong sector tailwind priced in. Wednesday's Cooper Companies (COO US) sits in healthcare, similarly flat at +0.1% median. Thursday carries most of the week's load: Donaldson (DCI US) and AeroVironment (AVAV US) report into industrials, the sector with the sharpest recent pullback at -1.5% median reaction across 576 names; Kroger (KR US) reports into consumer-defensive, also negative at -0.8% median; and Palo Alto Networks (PANW US) headlines a cluster of technology reports (Adobe, Guidewire, Nutanix, UiPath, SailPoint, Bitmine among them) that still nets to a flat sector read.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table at +6.6% median across 167 names, backed by real volume (2,629 news items) -- notable even though none of its members report this week. Alternative-asset-management (+2.9%, 6 tickers, 231 items) and copper (+2.6%, 6 tickers, 248 items) follow but run thin on coverage, so treat those two as directional rather than conclusive. Industrials (-1.5% median, 576 names, 6,810 items) is the most heavily-covered sector showing real weakness, and it's the one sector this week's calendar actually touches, via DCI and AVAV.
